name: How to Replace and Install a Bathroom Vanity Step by Step

step.name: Step 1: Shut off the water supply and drain existing lines
step.text: Close the hot and cold shutoff valves completely under the sink. Turn on the faucet handles to relieve line pressure, then place a catch bucket beneath the P-trap to capture standing water before disconnecting the drain assembly and flexible water lines.

step.name: Step 2: Remove the old vanity and inspect the exposed wall and floor
step.text: Back out the mounting screws securing the old cabinet to the wall studs, slice through old perimeter caulk with a utility knife, and ease the cabinet away. Check the exposed drywall and subfloor for water damage, mildew, or unlevel framing that needs patching before moving forward.

step.name: Step 3: Map wall studs and check for concealed utilities
step.text: Run a reliable stud finder along the mounting zone and mark framing centers clearly with a pencil. Double-check the wall area around plumbing vents and electrical switches to avoid piercing hidden wiring or vent pipes when driving mounting screws later.

step.name: Step 4: Position, shim, and anchor the new vanity cabinet
step.text: Slide the new cabinet into place, checking level along both the top rim and across the face. Insert wood shims under the base until it is perfectly plumb and level, then secure the cabinet frame into the wall studs using heavy-duty cabinet screws.

step.name: Step 5: Mount the sink and connect plumbing connections
step.text: Install the faucet and drain flange onto the basin before setting it, then attach the basin securely to the cabinet. Reconnect the P-trap and supply lines, open the water valves, and run water continuously to inspect every threaded joint for drips.
